target_customer: Shoppers in Ghana and Nigeria buying from US online retailers, and travellers flying home who earn money carrying items
problem: Shipping from the US to Ghana and Nigeria was slow and expensive. Shypmate, later Envyl, bought items for shoppers and had home bound travellers carry them, with a hand off at the airport.
business_model: Delivery fee per order with travellers paid 70 percent of Shypmate's fee

founders.name: Perry Ogwuche
founders.background_notes: YC page calls him founding engineer at Checkr Pay now; Techpoint (2019-10) says LinkedIn showed Amida; sources conflict.

founders.name: Tochukwu Okoro
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; Techpoint says he was the only co-founder left on LinkedIn in 2019.

founders.name: Chisom Ebinama
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by Techpoint; later left to work on a project called Views.

exit.reason: Techpoint (2019-10) calls it on indefinite hiatus or defunct; co-founder Chisom Ebinama said capital was the biggest challenge

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.what: Express courier shipping from the US to Ghana
competitors.traction_then: Incumbent courier; a $50 pair of shoes cost $250 to ship in Shypmate's test versus $25 via Shypmate

technical_complexity.rationale: A purchasing and matching web app was simple; the difficulty was trust, background checks and cross border logistics.

defensibility.rationale: The traveller network could be copied and shoppers could use informal relatives or couriers; the only edge was trust built over transactions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer appeared. Techpoint (2019-10) mentions Jumia only as a larger ecommerce player raising more money.

market_need_then: TechCrunch (2016-01-28) reported a price of $25 versus $250 for DHL on a test shipment and delivery in an average of three to five days, plus over 100 transactions within two months of testing per a later report.

branding.name_origin: Shypmate was renamed Envyl in April 2017 with the stated goal of expanding services; the origin of either name is not stated in sources found

rebrands.why: Company said the goal was expanding its services; the Medium post notes the company went quiet shortly after the rename

branding.community_and_virality: Coverage in Ghanaian and Nigerian tech press (Techpoint, TechCabal, Pulse Nigeria) and Medium blogs for the Shypmate name.

brand_strength.rationale: Shypmate had regional press attention, but the 2017 rename to a less intuitive invented name coincided with a pause and reduced order types.

pivots.from: Delivery to Ghana and Nigeria as Shypmate
pivots.to: Ghana only as Envyl, initially accepting orders only from Amazon
pivots.why: Founder said a startup needed to focus on one market

outcome_analysis: Shypmate launched in January 2016 from YC Winter 2016 with a travellers based delivery model for Ghana and Nigeria, renamed to Envyl in April 2017 and narrowed to Ghana with restricted retailers. A co-founder said capital was the biggest challenge, the team used credit cards and took other jobs, and Techpoint called it on hiatus or defunct in October 2019, with no outside round beyond the YC investment recorded.
